name: Edoardo Rolla
bio: Young Genoese seaman whom Wilde had written to ahead of his move from Switzerland to Genoa in the first week of April 1899, and hoped to find waiting for him there. Wilde described him to Robert Ross as 'a young lad, by name Edoardo Rolla, one of the sea-farers', with 'fair hair', 'always in dark blue'. No age, dates or other trace appear in the letter, and no record of whether the meeting took place was found in the pages read.
bio_note: Sole source: Wilde to Robert Ross, [early April 1899], Gland, Complete Letters (2000), p. 1140 (repo PDF 1186, printed folio confirmed on the rendered page image). The editors' general index reportedly lists him as 'Rolla, Edoardo (boy)', per the triage's mirror read - finding-only, not verified in the source. DATES: NONE RECORDED. Searched so far: the whole OCR mirror of the Complete Letters (2000) for every occurrence of the name, plus the edition's General Index; Frankel, Oscar Wilde: The Unrepentant Years (2017), repo PDF, the fullest scholarly account of the exile years; McKenna, The Secret Life of Oscar Wilde (2008) and Murray, Bosie (2020), repo PDFs. Frankel treats him at printed pp. 248 and 250 (repo PDF 262, 264) and indexes him as 'Rolla, Edoardo, 248, 250'; he offers only 'possibly a sailor or fisherman' and no dates. No birth or death date is recorded in any source consulted, and none is likely to be: the record preserves a first name (or a trade) in another man's correspondence and no surname to search by.
